artists.biography: Haken (/ˈheɪkən/) are an English progressive metal band formed in 2007 by multi-instrumentalist Richard Henshall, guitarist Matthew Marshall, and vocalist Ross Jennings. While Henshall, Marshall, and Jennings first had the idea of forming Haken in 2004, they opted to pursue their instruments and songwriting first. Upon recruiting other members three years later, they eventually released the demo Enter the 5th Dimension in 2008, signing with Sensory Records and releasing their first album Aquarius in 2010. As of 2020, they have released six studio albums, an EP, and two live albums.

perplexity.description:
The Mountain is the third studio album by English progressive metal band Haken, released on 2 September 2013 through Inside Out Music. The album marks a deliberate shift toward rawer, more emotionally focused songwriting while maintaining the band's signature progressive complexity. Recorded in 2012–2013 at The Crypt in London, the record features thematic depth centered on personal struggle and perseverance, with band members describing it as symbolic of both their artistic journey and the broader trials of life. Musically, the compositions balance intricate progressive arrangements with more accessible melodic passages, exemplified by tracks like "Because It's There," which incorporates a non-metal chorus that contrasts sharply with the album's heavier moments.

The Mountain proved to be a significant commercial and critical turning point for Haken, becoming the band's most popular album to date. The record garnered recognition from prominent figures in progressive music, with Dream Theater's Jordan Rudess and Mike Portnoy citing it among their top 10 albums of 2013, while Between the Buried and Me's Dan Briggs also praised the work. The album achieved notable accolades within the progressive rock community, winning first place in Prog Sphere's albums of 2013 and later ranking at number 54 on Prog Magazine's list of the 100 Greatest Prog Albums of All Time. The album's promotional music video for "Cockroach King," released in September 2013, remains the most viewed video on Haken's YouTube channel. This was the final album to feature bassist Thomas MacLean, marking the end of an era for the band's classic lineup.
